Subject: Re: RDW onboarding: VPC activation playbook + procurement items

Hi Markus / Redwood team,

Thanks for the intro — OmniHealth is ready to move forward with the private deployment (VPC) for our production inference workload. We have a tight go-live window: target environment activation week of Apr 15. Before we lock dates the procurement team needs a short checklist and any required PO language so we can push the SOW and payment.

High-level asks from our side:
- Exact list of account-level prerequisites (service accounts, IP ranges to allow, required firewall ports)
- Any network peering or interconnect prerequisites and expected public egress requirements
- Draft MOA/SOW and one-page pricing summary for dedicated capacity (monthly commit + burst)
- Evidence for SOC2 audit / encryption-at-rest details for our compliance team

I can share our network diagram and the cloud contacts (Amit is our NetEng lead). Can we schedule a 30-min tech+procure alignment next week?

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Patel
Head of Cloud Ops | OmniHealth

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Mar 2028 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RDW onboarding: VPC activation playbook + procurement items

Samira — thanks, this is great. Happy to align next week.

Quick answers up front and a proposed plan:
1) Procurement: I attached a one-page MOA (redwood_moa_v2.pdf) and a short pricing summary — let me know if ProcureIT needs alternate language or payment terms. We can also provide a completed W-9 and insurance certificate on request.
2) Network/account prerequisites (short checklist) — see below; Karthik will post the detailed runbook to Drive and we can walk through it during the call.

--- Minimal account/network prerequisites (summary) ---
- Customer VPC CIDR(s) and confirmed primary region + any peered regions
- Allocated public egress IP(s) or acceptance of our managed egress (list provided by Redwood)
- Firewall: allow outbound TCP 443 to redwood-control.redwood.com and UDP/TCP ports for private peering (we'll confirm exact ports in runbook)
- Service account(s) & IAM: a dedicated service account with ability to create/attach routes & security groups OR we can do cross-account peering with our managed role
- KMS/HSM: KMS key ARN for encryption-at-rest if customer-managed keys required
- Audit: retention window for audit logs (we support pushing logs to customer Cloud Storage)

I'll coordinate the technical run-through. Laura — can you pick 30-min slots on Apr 3-5 for tech + procurement? ProcureIT, if you can review the MOA and flag any redlines that speeds things up.

Best,
Markus Klein
Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_moa_v2.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira.patel@omnihealth.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Amit Roy <amit.roy@omnihealth.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Apr 2028 07:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RDW onboarding: VPC activation playbook + procurement items

Samira / Amit — looping in the technical checklist so we can be concrete on the call. Below are the items my team will validate during environment activation; if you can pre-send any CIDRs and expected peak concurrent sessions that helps sizing.

Technical validation checklist (to be completed during activation):
- Network topology: confirm CIDRs, route tables, NAT gateways, and any on-prem VPN/Direct Connect circuits
- Firewall rules: allow outbound to control plane + healthcheck endpoints; confirm TLS termination strategy
- Peering options: choose between IPsec VPN, Direct Interconnect, or AWS Transit Connect; note latency expectations
- DNS: provide private DNS delegation or conditional forwarding if using private endpoints
- Service accounts / roles: share role ARNs or service account emails; ensure required permissions: AttachNetworkInterface, CreateRoute, DescribeInstances (cloud specific names)
- Storage & KV caching: validate S3/GCS buckets for model artifacts and KMS keys for encryption; test object access from the private subnet
- Logging: configure Flow Logs and Cloud Audit logs to the retention specified (default 90 days)
- Quantization / model artifacts: confirm artifact size and L7 reverse proxy routing for model shards if >16GB

I'll prepare a short runbook and post to the Drive folder before the call. Two asks for today: (1) please upload the VPC diagram (already attached, thanks) and (2) confirm whether you require customer-managed KMS.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
